title: One Day at Disney California Adventure with Hana
summary: You will walk through one real day at the park. You will enter on Buena Vista Street, check three rides and their height limits, and eat a popular snack.

cover.alt: Hana points toward a red trolley while holding her parent's hand beside the teal and cream park entrance on a sunny morning.

blocks.title: Introduction
paragraphs: One question will follow you all day: is she tall enough for this ride? You will walk through one real day at the park. You will enter on Buena Vista Street, check three rides and their height limits, and eat a popular snack. Then you will choose Mickey ears and finish with World of Color.

blocks.title: Warm-up

items.prompt: Have you ever been to a theme park? What did you do first?
When you travel with a child, how do you choose what to do?
Do you like big, fast rides, or do you prefer shows and food?

blocks.title: Part 1: 8:00 a.m. — Through the Gate to Buena Vista Street
paragraphs: It is 8:00 a.m.  You and Hana walk up to the main gate. Before you go in, look up. The gate building has a big, rounded shape. It looks like the Pan-Pacific Auditorium, a famous old building.

When the park rebuilt this area, it moved the main gate further out. So the gate now stands in front of a whole new street. That street is Buena Vista Street, and it is the first thing you see inside.

Hana points to a red car moving slowly down the street. This is the Red Car Trolley, and it runs along Buena Vista Street. She wants to ride it right away. You smile and say, "Later." First, you want to plan the rides while the morning is still quiet.

blocks.title: Check: Part 1: 8:00 a.m. — Through the Gate to Buena Vista Street

items.prompt: What does the main gate look like, and what does Hana see on Buena Vista Street?
items.answer: The main gate looks like the Pan-Pacific Auditorium, a famous old building. On Buena Vista Street, Hana sees the Red Car Trolley, which runs along the street.

blocks.title: Part 2: 9:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. — Three Rides and Three Height Questions
paragraphs: At 9:00 a.m., you walk into Cars Land. Radiator Springs Racers comes from the 2006 film Cars. Six people sit in one car. Your car races another car, and the winner is random. You cannot plan to win. The ride was also very expensive to build. It is the most expensive attraction at Disneyland Resort and one of the most expensive in the world. Before you join the line, check the height sign at the entrance or in the app. Hana stands next to it to make sure.

At 10:30 a.m., you reach Guardians of the Galaxy – Mission: Breakout! Riders must be at least 40 inches (102 cm) tall.  But the park warns that this ride has big drops, and it is loud and scary. The park says it is best for teens and adults. So you must decide as her parent.

Next comes the Incredicoaster, a fast steel roller coaster. It launches forward instead of slowly climbing up. It is the only coaster at Disneyland Resort that turns riders upside down. It is also the fastest, at 55 mph (about 89 km/h). Riders must be at least 48 inches (122 cm) tall.
Lines can be long at busy rides. You may also hear the name Lightning Lane. Before you pay for anything, open the app. Read what Lightning Lane offers and what it costs on that day.

blocks.title: Check: Part 2: 9:00 a.m. to 11:00 a.m. — Three Rides and Three Height Questions

items.prompt: Which of the two rides with known height limits can Hana ride, and why?
items.answer: Hana can ride Guardians of the Galaxy – Mission: Breakout! because she is 115 cm and the limit is 102 cm. However, it is loud and scary, so you should still decide whether it is right for her. She cannot ride the Incredicoaster because the limit is 122 cm, and she is about 7 cm too short.

blocks.title: Useful phrases

rows.term: is my daughter tall enough for this ride?
rows.meaning: Ask a staff member before you wait in a long line.
rows.example: Excuse me, is my daughter tall enough for this ride?

rows.meaning: Ask this when a ride might be too much for a child.
rows.example: She loves fast rides, but how scary is it?

rows.term: How long is the wait right now?
rows.meaning: Ask about the line before you join it.
rows.example: Hi, how long is the wait right now?

rows.term: Thanks for telling me before we wait.
rows.meaning: Thank someone who saves you from a wasted wait.
rows.example: Oh, she's too short. Thanks for telling me before we wait.

blocks.title: Part 3: 12:30 p.m. — Lunch at Corn Dog Castle
paragraphs: You go to Corn Dog Castle, a snack stand. Its cheese stick is one of the park's most popular snacks.

The park does not print one price for everyone online, so look first. Before you order, check the price on the menu board or in the Disneyland app. You can also order and pay for food in the app. That can save time when the stand is busy. Today you order at the counter so Hana can watch.
There are bigger meals in the park too. Some guests make dining reservations for a sit-down lunch. But for a fast snack between rides, a stand like Corn Dog Castle works well.

blocks.title: Check: Part 3: 12:30 p.m. — Lunch at Corn Dog Castle

items.prompt: How can you find the price of the cheese stick before you order, and how can you pay?
items.answer: You can find the price on the menu board at the stand or in the Disneyland app. You can pay at the counter, or you can order and pay in the app.

blocks.title: Useful phrases

rows.meaning: Ask the price before you pay.
rows.example: Just water. How much is that?
Got it. Can I pay by card?

rows.meaning: Ask staff about a food you want to try.
rows.example: Is the cheese stick popular? I've never had one.

blocks.title: Part 4: 3:00 p.m. — Choosing Mickey Ears
paragraphs: At 3:00 p.m., you walk into a gift shop. Hana goes straight to the ear headbands. These are the famous Mickey and Minnie ears. A news report from October 2026 says these headbands now cost about $38.99. Before the price increase, they cost $36.99.

That is not cheap, so you think before you buy. One headband costs about $38.99. Two headbands cost about $77.98. Maybe Hana gets one pair, and you take photos of her wearing them. For a small gift for her friend at home, look at the price tag on each item. Then compare before you choose.

blocks.title: Check: Part 4: 3:00 p.m. — Choosing Mickey Ears

items.prompt: Why do you think carefully before you buy two headbands?
items.answer: Each headband costs about $38.99 after a price increase from $36.99. So two headbands cost about $77.98. That is a lot of money, so you compare before you choose.

blocks.title: Useful phrases

rows.term: How much are the Mickey ears?
rows.meaning: Ask the price of something you want to buy.
rows.example: Excuse me, how much are the Mickey ears?

rows.term: Can she try them on first?
rows.meaning: Ask to try something before you buy it.
rows.example: They look cute. Can she try them on first?

rows.meaning: Tell the staff member what you decided to buy.

blocks.title: Part 5: Evening — World of Color and the Walk Out
paragraphs: The park has character meet and greets with Mickey and others, along with parades and shows. Before the show, Hana meets Mickey. She shows him her new ears.
The big evening show is World of Color. The time can change from day to day, so check it in the Disneyland app. Then find your place early. Hana sits on your lap, tired but excited.

When the show ends, you walk back to the gate. Buena Vista Street is lit up at night, and Hana is quiet now. You pass the spot where the Red Car Trolley runs. You walk out under the big, rounded gate. She is holding your hand again, just like this morning.

blocks.title: Check: Part 5: Evening — World of Color and the Walk Out

items.prompt: How do you find out when World of Color starts?
items.answer: You check the show time in the Disneyland app because it can change from day to day. Then you arrive early to find a good place.

blocks.title: Scene: The Height Check at Guardians
paragraphs: You and Hana stand at the entrance to Guardians of the Galaxy – Mission: Breakout!
Your goal is to find out if Hana can ride. Learn how scary the ride is and ask about the Incredicoaster before you wait.

images.alt: Hana stands beside a ride-height marker while an attendant points to its red line and her parent watches outside a tall tower covered with pipes.

blocks.title: Conversation: The Height Check at Guardians

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Excuse me, is my daughter tall enough for this ride?

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Let's check. Hana, can you stand next to this sign? You need to be 40 inches, or 102 centimetres.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: I'm 115 centimetres!

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: Then you're tall enough. Nice! Just so you know, there are big drops, and it's very loud.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: How scary is it? She's only seven.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: The park says it's best for teens and adults. Some younger kids love it, and some get scared. You know her best.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Hana, do you still want to go?

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: Yes! I want to scream!

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: OK, she's ready. How long is the wait right now?

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: The wait time is on the sign by the entrance, and the Disneyland app shows it too. It changes during the day.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thanks. And after this, we want to try the Incredicoaster.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: For that one, riders need to be 48 inches, or 122 centimetres. So Hana can't ride it yet.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Oh, she'll be sad. Thanks for telling me before we wait.

turns.speaker: Jordan
turns.text: No problem. She'll be tall enough in a few years. Have fun in there!

blocks.title: Scene: Ordering at Corn Dog Castle
paragraphs: You stand at the counter of Corn Dog Castle. Maria is the cashier.
Your goal is to order two cheese sticks, check the price, pay and finish your order.

images.alt: Hana watches as her parent holds a bank card above the reader at a snack counter, where Maria gestures beside two golden battered snacks on sticks.

blocks.title: Conversation: Ordering at Corn Dog Castle

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Hi, two cheese sticks, please.

turns.speaker: Maria
turns.text: Sure! Anything to drink?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Just water. How much is that?

turns.speaker: Maria
turns.text: All the prices are on the board above me. Your total is on this screen now.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Got it. Can I pay by card?

turns.speaker: Maria
turns.text: Of course. Just tap here. Next time, you can also order and pay in the Disneyland app.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Good idea. Is the cheese stick popular? I've never had one.

turns.speaker: Maria
turns.text: Very popular. Lots of people come back for it. Is this your first visit?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Yes, we came from Japan. My daughter rode Guardians this morning.

turns.speaker: Maria
turns.text: Wow, she's brave! Here are your cheese sticks. Enjoy!

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thank you so much!

blocks.title: Scene: Choosing Ears in the Gift Shop
paragraphs: Hana is excited in front of the ear headbands.
Your goal is to check the price, let Hana try the ears and buy one pair.

images.alt: Hana lifts a pink ear headband with a bow above her head while her parent smiles beside a wooden display of headbands in a sunlit shop.

blocks.title: Conversation: Choosing Ears in the Gift Shop

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Excuse me, how much are the Mickey ears?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: The Mickey and Minnie headbands are about $38.99 each.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Oh, I think they were $36.99 before.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Yes, the price went up a little this year.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: Can I have Minnie ears, please?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: They look cute. Can she try them on first?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Of course. There's a mirror right here.

turns.speaker: Hana
turns.text: Look! I'm Minnie!

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: You look great. OK, just one pair today. I'll take these, please.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Wonderful choice. Would you like a bag, or will she wear them now?

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: She'll wear them, I'm sure. Do you have a small gift for her friend at home?

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: These small items are over here. Each one has a price tag, so you can compare.

turns.speaker: You
turns.text: Thanks. We'll look, then pay together.

turns.speaker: Sam
turns.text: Take your time. Enjoy the rest of your day, and take care in the park!

blocks.title: Speaking
paragraphs: Work with a partner. Tell the story of Hana's day in time order, from the morning to the night. Explain which rides Hana could ride and why. Then change roles. Your partner is a Cast Member, and you ask about one ride, one snack and one souvenir.

blocks.title: Final Reflection
blocks.intro: Hana's height decided many choices today, from Guardians to the Incredicoaster. The Disneyland app helped you check wait times, prices and show times before you decided. At night, you left through the same gate where your day began.

items.prompt: Would you let a seven-year-old ride a loud, scary ride if she was tall enough? Why?
Is $38.99 a fair price for a souvenir like Mickey ears?
Which part of this day would you enjoy most, and which part would be hardest?
